alternative_arguments.argument: MIT §25.3 and Stanford §9.2 supply independent state-space and impulse-response conventions. The local definition fixes dimensions, horizon, sample times, additive observation errors, and the one-index Markov convention explicitly.

Stanford §9.2 and MIT §25.2 supply independent observability-matrix and unobservable-kernel treatments. The local proof expands the known forced response, proves the exact kernel iff by rank-nullity, and derives the full-column-rank least-squares bound from SVD and projection suppliers.
Both full lecture-note treatments give the coordinate-change identity. The local proof verifies T^{-1}x_k for every sample by induction and then computes the output directly.

Stanford §9.2 explains Hankel-matrix realization and MIT Exercise 25.4 points to a Markov-parameter construction, but neither is claimed to supply the exact procedure. The local definition specifies the exact operation model, ranks, factors, pseudoinverses, block extraction, and all three outputs/failure statuses.

MIT §25.4 and Stanford §9.2 independently support the Hankel product and similarity method. The local proof establishes H0=O_qR_q and H1=O_qAR_q, constructs the invertible factor change, proves both Moore–Penrose inverse identities, and extracts Ahat, Bhat, and Chat.
